content.user_title: Integrate Apify Actors into Your Application
content.value_statement: Adding managed scraping and automation requires correct client setup, Actor inputs, and result handling. This skill provides practical Apify integration patterns for common application workflows.
actual_capabilities: Selects the correct apify-client package for JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python integrations.
Shows synchronous and asynchronous patterns for starting Apify Actor runs.
Retrieves structured dataset items and key-value store records from completed runs.
Provides REST API request patterns for languages without an official client.
Explains token configuration, error handling, pagination, timeouts, and client reuse.
Guides Actor discovery and input schema lookup through Apify Store or MCP tools.
limitations: Requires an Apify account, an API token, and access to the selected Actor.
Does not build or deploy new Apify Actors.
Actor inputs, outputs, pricing, and runtime behavior vary by Actor.
Does not determine whether a target website permits automated collection.

use_cases.title: Add Scraping to a Web Application
use_cases.description: Connect an existing JavaScript or TypeScript service to an Apify Actor and consume its dataset results.

use_cases.title: Automate Python Data Collection
use_cases.description: Run an Actor from a Python workflow, wait for completion, and pass extracted records into a pipeline.

use_cases.title: Integrate Apify Through REST
use_cases.description: Start runs, check status, and retrieve datasets from a language without an official Apify client.

prompt_templates.title: Install and Configure the Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Apify to my [JavaScript or Python] application. Show the correct package, secure APIFY_TOKEN setup, and a minimal connection example.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Actor and Read Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate Actor [actor ID] into this application. Use this input: [requirements]. Wait for completion and return paginated dataset items.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Asynchronous Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an asynchronous Apify workflow for [use case]. Start the Actor, preserve the run ID, handle failures, and retrieve results after completion.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Apify integration for production use. Add timeouts, pagination, structured error handling, client reuse, secret management, and Actor-specific input validation.

output_examples.input: Add the Apify web scraper to a TypeScript service and collect up to ten pages.
output_examples.output: A TypeScript integration plan with secure token configuration, Actor execution, dataset retrieval, and clear failure handling.

output_examples.input: Run an Actor asynchronously from Python and process its results later.
output_examples.output: A Python workflow that starts the run, stores its identifier, waits for completion, and retrieves paginated dataset records.

output_examples.input: Use Apify from a language without an official client.
output_examples.output: A REST integration outline covering authenticated run creation, status polling, and dataset retrieval.

best_practices: Store APIFY_TOKEN in an environment variable or managed secrets service.
Check the selected Actor input schema before constructing requests.
Set timeouts and paginate large datasets to control runtime and memory use.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode API tokens in source code or commit them to version control.
Do not install the apify package when the application only needs to call Actors.
Do not assume every Actor accepts the same input or returns the same output.

faq.question: Which package should an application install?
faq.answer: Install apify-client. The apify package is intended for building Actors, not calling them from an existing application.

faq.question: How should I provide the Apify token?
faq.answer: Use APIFY_TOKEN through an environment variable or secrets manager. Never place the token directly in application source.

faq.question: Can this skill help me choose an Actor?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Actor discovery through Apify MCP tools or the Apify Store and checking each Actor input schema.

faq.question: When should I use synchronous execution?
faq.answer: Use synchronous execution for short runs when the request can wait until the Actor finishes.

faq.question: How are Actor results retrieved?
faq.answer: Most structured results come from the run dataset. Files and screenshots may be stored in the run key-value store.

faq.question: Does the skill support languages beyond JavaScript and Python?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides REST API patterns for starting runs, checking status, and retrieving dataset items.
